name: Non-syndromic Longitudinal Limb Defect

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Non-syndromic Longitudinal Limb Defect Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of a congenital longitudinal deficiency affecting one or more limbs without associated syndromic features
No clinical or genetic evidence of syndromic conditions associated with limb defects
Radiographic evidence confirming longitudinal bone deficiency in affected limb(s)
Absence of family history of syndromic limb malformations

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met: congenital longitudinal limb deficiency without syndromic features, absence of syndromic diagnosis, and radiological confirmation of longitudinal bone deficiency.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may be performed to exclude syndromic causes but is not diagnostic for non-syndromic longitudinal limb defect.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital longitudinal deficiency of the radius
searchTerms: absence of forearm bone on thumb side

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital longitudinal deficiency of the ulna
searchTerms: absence of forearm bone on pinky side

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital longitudinal deficiency of the tibia
searchTerms: absence of tibia bone in lower leg

common.symptomName: Limited range of motion in affected limb joints
searchTerms: stiff joints in affected arm or leg

common.symptomName: Hypoplasia of digits adjacent to the longitudinal defect
searchTerms: reduced finger size near bone defect
small muscles in affected arm or leg

occasional.symptomName: Mild limb length discrepancy in contralateral limb
searchTerms: slight difference in opposite limb length

occasional.symptomName: Compensatory scoliosis secondary to limb length discrepancy
searchTerms: curved spine from uneven leg length
spine bending due to limb length difference

occasional.symptomName: Mild joint contractures adjacent to defect
searchTerms: slight tightness in joints next to limb problem
minor joint contractures close to defect
indentations on skin at affected limb

imaging: Radiographs showing longitudinal bone deficiency in radius, ulna, or tibia
MRI to assess soft tissue and muscle hypoplasia
Ultrasound prenatal detection of limb defects
genetic: Absence of pathogenic variants in genes associated with syndromic limb malformations
Negative chromosomal microarray for syndromic deletions or duplications
other: Physical examination confirming isolated limb defect without systemic involvement

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of syndromic features such as cardiac or hematological abnormalities
Genetic mutations in known syndromic genes (e.g., TBX5 in Holt-Oram syndrome)
Absent radius with associated hematological abnormalities

redFlags: Presence of systemic anomalies suggesting syndromic diagnosis
Progressive limb deformity beyond congenital presentation
Severe functional impairment of affected limb requiring urgent intervention
references: Orphanet: Non-syndromic Longitudinal Limb Defect - ORPHA:498457
Goldfarb CA, et al. Longitudinal Limb Deficiencies: Diagnosis and Management. J Hand Surg Am. 2019.
Temtamy SA, McKusick VA. The Genetics of Hand Malformations. Springer-Verlag, 1978.
